jobs.title: Media Buyer / Creative Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Media buying is now the easy part. In 2026, the buying itself is piping.
jobs.description:
Media buying is now the easy part.

In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.

So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.

Here's what "end to end" actually means here.

You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.

You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.

You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.

Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.

Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.

Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.

Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.

Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.

Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.

Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.

You're a fit if

You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.

You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.

You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.

You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.

You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.

You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.

Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.

You're not a fit if

  • "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.

Benefits

Why This Role Is Exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

We're looking for a highly organized, proactive Marketing Project Manager to build the operating system for our paid media team, and then run it.

Sweat Pants Agency manages around 57 brands and spends between $5M and $10M a month across Meta, Google, TikTok, and AppLovin. We're the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands from zero. Our average client stays with us for over three years.

Our email and SMS side is exceptionally well run. Project management there is tight, the templates exist, the dashboards are live, and nothing slips. Our paid media side is not there yet, and that's the job. This role is paid media only, so you won't be splitting your attention across two teams.

Roughly 25 to 30 accounts sit on the paid media side and are yours to keep in order. You'd be the first person in this seat, which means you're not inheriting a process. You're designing one.

The first things you'd own

We think in rocks, meaning the things that need pushing uphill. Here are ours, in priority order.

1. Capacity planning. Right now we don't have a real model for who is working on what, how loaded they are, or what happens when a new account lands. You'd build it: a live view of capacity across media buyers, designers, and video editors, with the ability to see an overload coming two weeks out instead of the day someone misses a deadline.

2. Creative workflow and process. Creative is our biggest bottleneck and it's cross functional. It spans our graphic design team, our video editors, and our media buyers who double as creative strategists. There's no single pipeline from request to delivery right now. You'd build it, run it, and be the person who guarantees we hit the creative volumes we owe clients every month.

3. Creators and UGC. We source creators constantly and there's no system behind it. You'd own sourcing across Billo, Backstage, email, and wherever else the right person is. That means negotiating rates and turnaround, tracking orders, managing usage rights so we never run an ad we've lost the rights to, tracking costs per account, and making sure markups land correctly on client invoices. If you haven't done this before, you should be genuinely comfortable asking a stranger for a better rate.

4. Client onboarding. We have a process and it needs refining, by someone who does this for a living rather than by me. Account access collection (Meta Business Manager, Google Ads, Klaviyo, Shopify, TikTok), ClickUp setup, reporting and dashboard configuration, so every launch feels identical.

What you'd do day to day

  • Run ClickUp as the single source of truth. Build and maintain templates, recurring tasks, intake forms, automations, and dashboards. Every account has a current status and a named owner, always.
  • Own capacity planning across the paid media team and flag overload before it becomes a missed deliverable.
  • Track every creative deliverable from request to delivery, including revisions and approvals, and QA the work before it reaches a client.
  • Source, negotiate with, and manage creators. Track orders, usage rights, and costs.
  • Own client onboarding end to end and standardize it so every launch runs the same way.
  • Build landing pages and advertorials using Claude Code from time to time.
  • Make sure client reporting and dashboards are set up correctly and stay accurate for every account.
  • Build internal tools, automations, and living SOPs using AI so the whole team runs faster and the same way every time.
  • Catch gaps in communication and delivery before they escalate, and drive follow ups to closure.
  • Schedule and coordinate recurring client and internal meetings, capture action items, and make sure they actually get done.
  • Flag at risk accounts early and escalate.

About the landing pages

We don't sell landing pages as a service. We build them anyway, because a weak page is the most common reason good creative doesn't convert, and waiting on a client's dev team costs us weeks.

Our media buyers already build pages this way. You'd do the same: advertorials, presell pages, and landing page variants built with Claude Code off existing templates and shipped to Shopify or the client's stack. You don't need to be an engineer and you won't be architecting anything from scratch. You need to be someone who can take a brief, work with AI to build the page, QA it, and ship it, and who finds that interesting rather than terrifying.

How we work, and please read this part carefully

This is the part most job posts leave out, and it's the part that actually determines whether you'd be happy here.

We give a lot of autonomy and we mean it. Nobody here is on a time clock and nobody ever will be. If I have to think about what you're doing with your hours, we've already lost. I judge outcomes, not activity.

The flip side is that I'm not a gatekeeper. One of the biggest red flags for me is someone who asks a lot of permission questions. Can I change this, should I do that. No. Just do it and show me. If you need a company card to solve something, you'll have one. You have full trust on day one. It's only ever lost, never earned.

Ownership is the thing we care about most. "That wasn't my role" is a disqualifier here. If creative is the bottleneck on an account, you go fix creative, whether or not it was in your scope. We've all done work outside our lane to get the result.

We judge the first 30 days harshly. We're looking for you to take action early and show that you're self directed. We usually know quickly, and it rarely turns around. What I can tell you is that people who make it past that point almost never leave. Our team retention is exceptional.

Mistakes are fine. Patterns aren't. You'll never hear me raise my voice. When something breaks we look at the process, not the person. My Slack tagline is "everything's my fault." But if the same thing breaks repeatedly, that's a fit problem.

My job is to protect the team. We have let go of clients for being unkind to our people and we'll do it again. I ask you to put clients first, and if there's ever a problem, tell me, because I'll put you first.

I like being wrong. Tell me there's a better way. Nothing here is sacred and everything can change.

Where this goes

On our email side, project management became the pipeline into strategy. Several of our email strategists started as PMs. We're building the same path on paid media. If you want to end up as a media buyer or creative strategist, this is the seat that gets you there, and you'll get your hands dirty along the way, writing creative briefs, launching ads, and sitting in on account reviews.

If you'd rather stay in operations and own this function as it grows, that works too. Tell us which one you want.

Our mission is simple: be the no BS agency partner you love working with.

Requirements

Skills

  • Elite organization and follow through. You close loops without being chased.
  • You build project management systems, you don't just work inside them. Hands on experience standing up or substantially rebuilding a system in ClickUp, Asana, or Monday, including spaces, custom fields, templates, statuses, intake, automations, and dashboards. We will ask you to walk us through one you personally designed.
  • Highly AI enabled, and comfortable building rather than just prompting. You've used Claude, Claude Code, or a comparable agentic tool to actually make something, whether that's a page, a dashboard, an automation, or an internal tool. Tell us what it was and what it replaced. This is non negotiable and we test it.
  • Proactive problem solver who anticipates gaps rather than reacting to them.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. This role is partly client facing, so English fluency is required.
  • Comfortable negotiating. A meaningful part of this role is talking to creators about rates, timelines, and deliverables.
  • Comfortable juggling many concurrent projects and context switching across accounts.
  • Detail obsessed, with a high standard for quality and accuracy.

Requirements

  • 2+ years in project management, creative operations, account management, or agency operations, preferably in a marketing or creative agency setting.
  • Proven ability to manage timelines and deliverables across many projects at once.
  • Hands on experience building and managing a project management system in ClickUp or a comparable tool. This is a hard requirement.
  • Demonstrated AI building, not just AI usage. This is a hard requirement.
  • Working hours with meaningful overlap with US business hours.
  • Bonus: experience with paid media or DTC ecommerce.
  • Bonus: experience sourcing and managing UGC creators or influencers.
  • Bonus: familiarity with Shopify, Figma, or front end tooling.

Benefits

Why Sweatpants Agency?

We’re not your typical agency. We’re the only agency behind multiple INC #1 fastest-growing companies from scratch. We thrive on innovation, creative problem-solving, and delivering results that make our clients say, “Wow.”If you’re ready to join a team that values your skills, pushes you to grow, and gives you the freedom to innovate, then we want to hear from you.

Digital Solutions Practice

Michael Baker International's Digital Solutions practice designs, builds, and operates the cloud, data, and technology platforms that enable MBI's mission-critical engineering and consulting work. With expertise spanning multi-cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, application delivery, and AI/ML enablement, the Digital Solutions team drives the digital transformation of MBI's internal and client-facing capabilities in support of the company's Vision 2030 strategic roadmap. The practice supports a broad portfolio of engineering disciplines—transportation, infrastructure, water, environment, and federal services—by delivering scalable, secure, and resilient technology foundations that accelerate project delivery and operational excellence. Guided by principles of automation, infrastructure as code, and DevOps best practices, Digital Solutions maintains a modern technology environment that supports thousands of professionals across the enterprise and positions MBI as a technology-forward leader in the architecture, engineering, and construction industry.

What We're Looking For

Michael Baker International is seeking a Senior Cloud DevOps Engineer to join our Digital Solutions team in a fully remote capacity. In this hands-on senior role, you will design, build, and maintain MBI's enterprise cloud infrastructure across Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services collaborating with the VP of Product, VP of Infrastructure, and CISO to align cloud platforms with product delivery, operational reliability, and security compliance. You will play a pivotal role in advancing MBI's Vision 2030 digital transformation strategy—driving CI/CD automation, Infrastructure as Code practices, AI/ML infrastructure enablement, and platform engineering across the enterprise.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement enterprise-scale multi-cloud infrastructure across Microsoft Azure and AWS, with a focus on Azure as the primary platform, ensuring high availability, fault tolerance, and performance for all environments and services.
  • Develop and deploy Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform as the primary tool, with proficiency in ARM/Bicep and AWS CloudFormation to standardize cloud provisioning, enforce configuration governance, and enable repeatable, version-controlled deployments.
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions and GitHub as the primary version control system to automate build, test, and deployment processes aligned with product delivery timelines.
  • Establish comprehensive monitoring, observability, and incident response capabilities using Azure Monitor, CloudWatch, Datadog, and Prometheus to uphold enterprise SLAs, detect anomalies, and drive continuous reliability improvement.
  • Manage Azure infrastructure fundamentals including subscriptions, tenants, VNets, VWAN, Network Security Groups, and firewalls to establish secure, scalable, and compliant cloud foundations.
  • Drive cloud cost optimization through FinOps practices—leveraging Azure Cost Management and AWS Cost Explorer to right-size resources, implement governance frameworks, and eliminate waste across the enterprise.
  • Enforce security and compliance standards across cloud environments in partnership with the CISO, implementing IAM controls, network segmentation, encryption, and zero-trust architecture aligned with SOC 2, FedRAMP, and CMMC requirements.
  • Serve as MBI's primary technical liaison with Microsoft Azure and AWS—managing vendor partnerships, coordinating architecture reviews, and aligning the cloud roadmap with provider capabilities and strategic initiatives.
  • Write automation scripts and tools in Python, Bash, or PowerShell to streamline infrastructure deployment, system integration, and DevOps workflows.

What You Need to Succeed

Required:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience designing, building, and managing cloud infrastructure in production environments across both Microsoft Azure and AWS
  • Deep expertise in Infrastructure as Code including Terraform, Azure Resource Manager/Bicep, and AWS CloudFormation, with demonstrated proficiency in modular design, state management, and environment promotion strategies
  • Proficiency in CI/CD pipeline development and maintenance using GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, or AWS CodePipeline
  • Strong scripting and coding abilities in Python, Bash, and PowerShell for automation, system integration, and DevOps workflow development
  • Proven experience with cloud security implementation including IAM, zero-trust architecture, network segmentation, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FedRAMP)
  • Experience with cloud cost management, FinOps practices, and cloud governance frameworks at enterprise scale
  • Proficiency with monitoring and observability tools including Azure Monitor, AWS CloudWatch, Datadog, Prometheus, and Grafana
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to engage technical and non-technical stakeholders including CTO-level executives
  • Preferred: Hands-on experience with Kubernetes (AKS, EKS), Docker, and container orchestration in production environments
  • Preferred: Experience building and managing cloud infrastructure for AI/ML workloads including GPU compute, vector databases, and model serving pipelines
  • Preferred: Experience with platform engineering practices and internal developer platform (IDP) development
  • Preferred: Professional certifications in AWS (Solutions Architect Professional), Microsoft Azure (Solutions Architect Expert), or HashiCorp (Terraform Associate)

Preferred:

  • Hands-on experience migrating infrastructure and workloads from AWS to Azure.
  • Experience with PowerShell, Ansible, or other infrastructure automation frameworks.
  • Expertise in Kubernetes (AKS, EKS) and Docker container orchestration in production environments.
  • Experience building and managing cloud infrastructure for AI/ML workloads including GPU compute, vector databases, and model serving pipelines.
  • Professional certifications in AWS (Solutions Architect Professional), Microsoft Azure (Solutions Architect Expert), or HashiCorp (Terraform Associate).
  • Experience with cloud cost management, FinOps practices, and governance frameworks at enterprise scale.
  • Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) background with exposure to SLI/SLO definition and incident response frameworks.
  • Experience with platform engineering practices and internal developer platform (IDP) development.

Compensation

The approximate compensation range for this position is $110,000 to $190,000. This compensation range is a good faith estimate for the position at the time of posting. Actual compensation is dependent upon factors such as education, qualifications, experience, skillset, and physical work location.

The Global Legal Project and Value Pricing Manager plays a critical operational role on global client engagements spanning more than 50 countries. Working with senior legal, business and client leadership, the role manages day-to-day budgeting and coordination of services, ensuring consistent execution across teams, ALSPs and technology platforms. The Manager also leads legal service delivery efficiency initiatives and the integration of AI and automation into financial workflows, turning manual processes into intelligent, scalable systems and serving as a trusted operational partner for the Firm’s most strategically important client relationships.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead annual budget planning and monitoring for complex, value‑based fee arrangements, ensuring real‑time visibility into financial performance.

  • Develop, manage, and report on multi‑jurisdictional matter budgets in coordination with the Global Billing Coordinator, ensuring compliance with client OCGs.
  • Manage the end‑to‑end project lifecycle for large, cross‑border client programs across 50+ countries, with clear governance and reporting.
  • Coordinate multi‑disciplinary teams (internal lawyers, local counsel, ALSPs, technology) across time zones and workstreams.

  • Support client relationship management through regular reporting, governance meetings, and preparation of materials for partner and executive forums.
  • Prepare communications and presentations to leadership with excellent strategic analysis and insights.
  • Identify, implement, and embed AI‑powered and legal technology tools to improve efficiency, quality, and matter management.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of financial management/pricing and legal project management experience in a law firm, in-house legal department, or ALSP environment.
  • Deep expertise in legal matter budgeting, AFAs, outside counsel guideline compliance, and/or legal financial reporting.
  • Exceptional communication skills with the ability to prepare and present to senior client and firm leadership.
  • Excellent proficiency in Excel, SharePoint, use of CoPilot (or similar) and AI tools for project management and workflow.

Preferred

  • Demonstrated experience managing multi-jurisdictional legal budgets with meaningful budget responsibility
  • Experience in a dedicated client service or embedded legal ops roles.
  • Exposure to cross-border regulatory, M&A, or commercial matters.
  • Working knowledge of legal AI platforms such as Harvey, Legora, or comparable tools.

Key Competencies:

  • Financial Acumen
  • Project Leadership
  • AI Fluency
  • Stakeholder Management
  • Data & Analytics

Benefits

  • Remuneration and benefits package will reflect the successful candidates experience and country where hired.

Please apply with an English resume

Salary range: US$80,000–US$160,000 gross annually, depending on experience and qualifications.

jobs.title: Strengthening SUNCASA Evidence for GESI-Responsive Urban Nature-based Solutions:
jobs.excerpt: BackgroundThe Scaling Urban Nature-based Solutions for Climate Adaptation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SUNCASA) project aims to enhance climate resilience, gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and biodiversity protection across three cities: Dire Dawa (Ethiopia), Kigali (Rwanda), and Johannesburg (South Africa).
jobs.description:
Background

The Scaling Urban Nature-based Solutions for Climate Adaptation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SUNCASA) project aims to enhance climate resilience, gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and biodiversity protection across three cities: Dire Dawa (Ethiopia), Kigali (Rwanda), and Johannesburg (South Africa). This initiative is led by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) in partnership with the World Resources Institute, together with local partners. The main objective of SUNCASA is to address climate-induced risks (e.g., floods, landslides, and soil erosion) by implementing GESI-responsive nature-based solutions (NbS). This is aimed at strengthening the resilience of urban communities, watersheds, and biodiversity from the impacts of climate change, while reducing barriers to NbS participation among women and the underrepresented groups. This would be achieved through targeted interventions such as afforestation and reforestation programs, agroforestry, urban greening, and establishment of vegetated buffer zones in affected areas. The project was launched in late 2023, and implementation will be completed by late 2026.

Despite growing interest and investment in urban NbS, relatively little evidence exists regarding how gender-responsive approaches to NbS influence project effectiveness, sustainability, governance, and equity outcomes. Gender-responsive approaches to NbS under SUNCASA are actions to protect, sustainably manage, and restore natural or modified ecosystems that address and challenge gender and social inequalities to promote equity, justice, and inclusion. This intersectional approach also considers diverse knowledge systems, including local knowledge, that result in equitable benefits from decision making and participation in NbS.

As the project nears completion, SUNCASA offers a unique opportunity to strengthen the evidence base on how GESI-responsive NbS contribute to larger climate adaptation and biodiversity protection outcomes in urban contexts. To this end, IISD seeks to engage an external monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) consultancy team to conduct a theory-based end-of-project evaluation to assess progress toward achieving selected SUNCASA outcomes.

The evaluation will employ theory-based mixed methods, such as key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs) for different sets of actors from each city. Deliverables of this opportunity will include a final external evaluation report (reporting against select outcomes) and communications products to showcase SUNCASA’s early impact/outcomes. Given the short project timeline of 3 years, this evaluation will focus on assessing evidence that supports the pathways of change hypothesized by SUNCASA and early signs of impact and sustainability from the project rather than looking for long-term impacts or effectiveness.

This RFP outlines the scope, objectives, and deliverables for engaging a MEL consultancy team for evaluation data collection and final deliverables.

Objective of the Assignment

This evaluation will assess the end-of-project progress toward achievement of selected SUNCASA intermediate and immediate outcomes that targeted decision-makers and local implementing partners participating in the project. Using mixed methods, a theory-based final evaluation report (including thematic case studies as part of the final report) will be developed to assess SUNCASA’s achievements in reaching selected outcomes. This assignment also requests an interim 2-pager communications product prepared to illustrate the early results and lessons from SUNCASA based on the evaluation, to support discussions at key events taking place in October/November 2026. Lastly, a shorter report will also be developed to showcase high-level results from the final report. Specifics regarding the assignment deliverables are provided in Section 3 of this RFP.

The 2-pager has a specific objective, audience and timeline intended for distribution at the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP). This deliverable will be developed first based on validated high-level, available results, with the final report and derived version to be completed at the end of the assignment. Therefore, the assignment includes a total of three (3) written deliverables, as outlined in Section 7 of this RFP. Appendix A presents the list of outcomes to be evaluated and proposed evaluation questions. The consultancy team is expected to review and revise the evaluation questions in collaboration with the IISD team prior to finalizing the evaluation.

As the SUNCASA project has existing quantitative and qualitative data sources, the consultancy team can use existing SUNCASA data as secondary data sources. Existing data includes

• NbS monitoring data (quarterly data on hectares restored, trees and buffer zone plants planted, debris removal, etc.);
• household-level perceived socio-economic and adaptive capacity data (final survey results from community stakeholders);
• community- and household-level stories of change (qualitative one-pagers from participating NbS workers and community members impacted by SUNCASA);

jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD94957

Position Overview

At Autodesk, we are pioneers in 3D design, engineering, and entertainment software, building tools that empower some of the most creative minds on the planet to solve real-world problems. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Glassdoor, and others as a top place to work, we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where innovation and creativity thrive.

Autodesk's Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) Data organization is seeking an experiencedSoftware Architectto join the AEC Data team and define the cloud-native services and distributed-systems architecture that power the AEC Data Model (AECDM) and the many services around it.

Data is the domain, but the role is fundamentally one of cloud and services architecture — APIs, service contracts, integrations, distributed-systems design, and the connected data model that ties them together — spanning multiple teams. It is not a data-warehouse or analytics-specialist role.

The AEC Data organization is building the foundational data infrastructure behind Autodesk's vision for connected construction: the platforms, services, and unified data models that span the entire built-asset lifecycle, from design and construction through operation and maintenance. This work enables the continuous flow of AEC data (3D models, 2D drawings, issue tracking, cost, sensor streams, and more) across Autodesk products and third-party integrations. The architect will help shape the next generation of capabilities for the Autodesk Forma Industry Cloud, collaborating with software architects, domain experts, and product teams across Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, Autodesk Construction Cloud, and Autodesk Forma.

This is a senior individual-contributor role on an established architecture track, reporting to the Distinguished Architect of the AEC Data team, who also serves as the Lead Software Architect. The primary responsibility is to shape how multiple teams design and build — through standards, reference architectures, ADRs, and design-review governance — rather than to own a single service. The exact focus flexes to your strengths and organizational need.

Responsibilities

  • API Design & Evolution: Design and evolve API surfaces across the AEC Data services — resource modeling, addressing, versioning and backward-compatible evolution, query APIs, and unifying overlapping surfaces into a single coherent contract.

  • System Architecture: Define and evolve cross-team, cloud-native architecture across the AEC Data services; design distributed systems including service contracts and event-driven flows.

  • Schema Design & Evolution: Design, document, and evolve data schemas for AEC domain entities (buildings, infrastructure, spaces, systems, components, relationships) — including semantic models, property sets, classification systems, and relationship hierarchies. Own versioning, backward/forward compatibility, deprecation, and migration; maintain the schema registry, validation rules, and quality checks.

  • Standards & Governance: Establish standards, reference architectures, and reusable components; author architecture proposals and decision records (ADRs) for review by a cross-org architecture council, and run cross-team design reviews.

  • Prototyping & Feasibility: Evaluate alternative architectural directions through modeling and prototyping, de-risking key decisions before broad adoption.

  • Mentorship & Technical Leadership: Mentor engineers and fellow architects on emerging and established technologies and on architectural practice; grow technical depth across teams.

  • Reliability & Performance: Ensure reliability, security, and performance of systems; define SLOs and drive observability (metrics, tracing, logging).

  • Communication: Communicate architecture with clear views and diagrams (e.g., C4) and executive-ready narratives; produce comprehensive documentation and onboarding materials.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, or equivalent experience.

  • 10+ years designing cloud-native, distributed systems, including 5+ years at cross-team architect altitude (Software Architect, Principal Engineer, Staff+, or equivalent). Title is flexible; scope of impact is the primary consideration.

  • Deep expertise in cloud services (ideally AWS), API/service design, and distributed-systems patterns (microservices, event-driven, resilience).

  • Solid grounding in data modeling and schema design — including schema definition languages (e.g., JSON Schema), versioning, and backward/forward-compatibility and evolution strategies — as applied both to standalone data schemas and to API contracts. Specialist data-warehouse or analytics architecture is not required.

  • Excellent knowledge of software design and architecture patterns.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across teams outside the candidate's direct management.

  • Strong leadership and mentoring skills, with a track record of guiding and growing diverse, cross-functional teams.

  • Mastery of conveying complex ideas concisely and persuasively, with excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills across a range of stakeholders.

  • Ability to collaborate with a global team.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred qualifications are a menu rather than a checklist: depth in a few core areas matters more than breadth across all of them. The emerging AI/ML capabilities below are advantageous and can be developed on the job; they are not prerequisites.

Core:

  • Cloud Services: AWS and its core services (EC2, ECS, Lambda, API Gateway, S3, DynamoDB, RDS).

  • Distributed Systems: Domain-driven service decomposition, data consistency patterns (CQRS, event sourcing, sagas), and multi-tenant/multi-region design.

  • API & Service Design: REST API design and evolution; GraphQL (including federation).

  • Database Architecture: Relational and NoSQL (e.g., DynamoDB, PostgreSQL).

  • Observability/SRE: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, metrics/SLOs for data services.

Bonus:

  • Semantic Technologies: Knowledge graphs, RDF/OWL, or property graphs — particularly relevant to the connected/semantic AECDM.

  • BIM Expertise: Building Information Modeling concepts, Revit families, or similar parametric modeling systems.

  • AI Systems: RAG, agents/MCP, agentic orchestration (LangGraph, Semantic Kernel), LLM observability, and data governance / AI safety (PII, prompt-injection, content filtering).

  • Domain-Specific AI for AEC: BIM/IFC extraction, CAD or point-cloud processing.

  • Event-Driven Architectures: Kafka or Kinesis; schema registries (Confluent, AWS Glue); exactly-once processing.

  • AEC Domain Knowledge: Experience in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction industry; familiarity with industry standards (IFC, COBie, gbXML, CityGML, LandXML, UniFormat, OmniClass). Domain onboarding is provided.

About the Team

The AEC Data team is building the AEC Data Model (AECDM) to enable better AECO (Architecture, Engineering, Construction, Operations) outcomes through more useful, connected, and accessible data. Its scope spans data services and APIs, product and design-tool integrations, and lifecycle/asset data across multiple teams — enabling the seamless flow of information across Autodesk products and third-party integrations so that AEC professionals can make better decisions with better data.

Why Join Us

  • Shape the future of AEC data platforms and standards at an industry-leading company.

  • Design systems and schemas used by millions of architects, engineers, and construction professionals worldwide.

  • Collaborate with world-class software architects and engineers across Autodesk's AEC portfolio.

  • Contribute to open standards and interoperability initiatives that benefit the entire industry.

  • Join a team that values technical excellence, innovation, and continuous learning.

Learn More

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

Position Overview:
The Senior Compliance Systems Analyst supports compliance-related system and process initiatives by serving as the day-to-day subject matter resource for assigned regulatory areas. This role is responsible for evaluating regulatory requirements, conducting first-pass research and analysis, helping design how requirements should function within the loan origination system and related workflows, and supporting the implementation of compliance-related changes. This role serves as a compliance subject-matter expert for designated LOS functionality, helping to establish, maintain, and continuously improve system behavior in alignment with regulatory requirements and internal policies. The Senior Compliance Systems Analyst operates at a level above pure testing execution by owning assigned workstreams, drafting and refining requirements, coordinating with stakeholders, and helping move changes from analysis through implementation and validation. This role partners closely with Legal, Technology, Operations, and Compliance leadership to ensure requirements are translated into practical, compliant business and system behavior.

Job Responsibilities:
• Serve as the primary compliance subject matter resource for assigned regulatory areas (for example, TILA, RESPA, TRID, and the SAFE Act, among others) and act as the day-to-day owner of related analysis, requirements, testing support, and implementation activities.

• Conduct first-pass regulatory research and issue analysis, identify open questions or gray areas, and prepare work products for attorney or executive compliance review and sign-off.
• Translate regulatory and business requirements into clear business, system, and procedural requirements that Technology, Operations, and other stakeholders can understand and execute.
• Help design how regulatory requirements should function within the loan origination system, including rules, fields, logic, workflows, outputs, and related operational impacts.
• Own assigned compliance-related changes from initial analysis through implementation and validation.

• Design and, when appropriate, execute test scenarios for assigned regulatory areas; review test results and defect findings; and identify gaps or issues requiring follow-up testing, requirement clarification, or escalation.
• Guide QA resources by clarifying expected behavior and refining test scenarios, while remaining directly involved in testing assigned regulatory areas to confirm that observed system behavior satisfies the underlying requirement.

  • Document requirements, interpretations, decisions, findings, and implementation outcomes in a clear and organized manner that supports audit, examination, and internal review needs.
    • Track open questions, exceptions, and dependencies related to assigned work and proactively follow through with stakeholders to keep items moving toward resolution.

    • Identify opportunities to improve processes, requirements templates, testing approaches, or documentation practices to strengthen the overall compliance change process.
    • Serve as the ongoing compliance owner for assigned LOS functionality, helping ensure rules, workflows, disclosures, and documents remain aligned with current regulatory requirements and internal policies.
    • Evaluate questions or concerns regarding existing compliance logic raised by internal stakeholders and, as applicable, external lenders, and determine whether clarification, additional testing, or updates are needed.
    • Support continuous improvement of LOS compliance by identifying enhancement opportunities, updating requirements, and partnering with stakeholders to implement and validate changes over time.

• Relevant education, training, certifications, or experience in compliance, mortgage operations, business analysis, legal support, quality assurance, or a related field.

• Experience performing regulatory research, compliance analysis, requirements drafting, testing support, or implementation support within mortgage or financial services environments, preferred.

The Shopping AI team is at the heart of Zillow Group’s mission to create a seamless digital real estate marketplace. About the role

As an Applied Scientist, you will help drive the next generation of ranking, recommendation, and generative AI systems for Zillow’s home-shopping experience. Your work will directly impact how millions of users discover and shop for homes, as you research, design, and deploy innovative machine learning models that power key product features. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to deliver solutions that make home shopping more intuitive, personalized, and efficient.

You Will Get To

  • Research, design, and prototype new machine learning models for Zillow’s consumer products, including search, ranking, recommendations, and notifications.

  • Lead the full model lifecycle: from ideation and offline experimentation on large datasets to online deployment, A/B testing, and ongoing performance monitoring.

  • Develop and test novel modeling approaches, such as deep learning architectures and large language models (LLMs), to improve the home-shopping experience.

  • Apply cutting-edge AI techniques, including LLM-based retrieval and RAG-style systems, to create more natural and conversational property search experiences.

  • Optimize how and when homes are displayed to users, ensuring relevance and context in every interaction.

jobs.excerpt: Who Are We? Xcelirate develops technologically-advanced platforms which are accessed by thousands of users every minute!
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Xcelirate develops technologically-advanced platforms which are accessed by thousands of users every minute! We are proud to offer a workplace where the sharpest developers come together to strategically plan and swiftly execute practices which see us maintain our existing market dominance and attain global expansion. We owe our success to our customers who have seen us grow across a decade, and our talented team who have made that growth possible.

What are we looking for?

You're a Principal-Level Full-Stack Engineer. You haven't just been around the block - you helped decide which blocks were worth building, and which ones should've been bulldozed early.

At this point, programming languages don’t really impress you anymore. You treat them as tools that translate intent into something a compiler or interpreter can run, choosing them pragmatically, discarding them without nostalgia, and never confusing syntax or novelty with actual progress.

You’ve been around long enough to remember when PHP constructors shared their class names, when exceptions were returned instead of thrown, and when Yeoman, Underscore, and CoffeeScript felt like the obvious future. More importantly, you also learned when to stop using those awful, awful, creations.

Despite all that experience, you’ve stayed deeply hands-on, and you’ve never been particularly interested in drifting into management just because that seemed like the default next step. You’re still happiest close to the code.

You bring a distinctly stoic approach to your work. You don’t panic when systems misbehave, you don’t chase drama, and you don’t confuse urgency with importance.

When you join a project, things tend to settle down. Code becomes easier to reason about, systems start to feel calmer, and decisions get clearer. That sense of clarity tends to spread to the people around you, and without any formal mentoring process, they start picking things up simply by working alongside you.

You have a solid, intuitive understanding of hot-path optimization, speculative execution, and lazy initialization, and you’re occasionally surprised that these simple concepts aren’t more widely understood.

And the homelab experiments you keep running at home, purely because you’re curious and can’t help yourself? We definitely want to hear about those.

If reading this feels a little too familiar, this role is likely to be a very good fit.

What will you be doing?

  • Manage your own time while adhering to priorities set by the company.
  • Own complex engineering problems end-to-end, from problem framing and design through to delivery and iteration.
  • Take responsibility for critical areas of the platform, ensuring they remain reliable, performant, and maintainable.
  • Build new features and improve existing ones across our platforms.
  • Refactor legacy and modern codebases pragmatically, balancing long-term health with delivery needs.
  • Write tests (unit, integration, and end-to-end) to ensure software reliability.
  • Be involved in every phase of the software lifecycle, from ideation to deployment.
  • Participate in (and at times lead) deep technical discussions, helping drive sound decisions and trade-offs.
  • Work hands-on across backend and frontend systems, stepping in wherever the problem lives.
  • Identify inefficiencies and help streamline workflows, reducing unnecessary work.
  • Collaborate closely with other senior engineers, raising the bar through example rather than authority
  • Take ownership of your work, ensuring high-quality results and maintainable solutions.

Requirements

What will you bring along?

  • 15+ years hands-on experience building and maintaining complex web applications
  • Clear technical communication; able to explain and defend design decisions to senior engineers and non-engineers alike
  • Expert PHP developer (12+ years); Symfony or equivalent frameworks
  • 10+ years modern JavaScript; React or Vue (Next/Nuxt a plus)
  • Expert level knowledge in at least one more programming language (Python a plus)
  • Full-stack architecture expertise: monoliths, services, and hybrids
  • Power user cloud deployment and scaling (AWS preferred) experience and abilities
  • Expert Linux user; including daily containerized workflows with Docker
  • Expert in infrastructure automation: Terraform, Ansible
  • Power user level CI/CD pipeline and release workflow ownership
  • Experience in automated testing: unit, integration, E2E; TDD where appropriate
  • Expert level knowledge in and around web security fundamentals: auth, authorization, data protection, secure coding
  • Legacy + modern codebase fluency; ability to work on incremental modernization
  • Strong independent technical ownership and accountability

We are always looking for the best candidates, so if you think you would be a good fit even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we would love to hear from you!

Benefits

How We Support Our Contractors

  • An annualised rate of €139,000 + retention bonus scheme: Competitive contractor rate with a generous bonus paid every 6 months based on your time with us.

ABOUT YOUR NEW ROLE

Do you enjoy writing and want to build a career in sports digital media? The Sporting News is seeking an ambitious, motivated and creative recent college graduate for a paid six-month content producer internship from August 2026 through February 2027.

This is a hands-on editorial role supporting The Sporting News and its growing network of media and commercial partnerships. You will write content for Sporting News platforms as well as regional sports network partners, including NESN and SportsNet Pittsburgh (SNP), producing coverage tailored to national, Boston and Pittsburgh audiences.

You will create content across a wide range of topics and formats, from breaking news and live-event coverage to evergreen, lifestyle and affiliate content. No two days will look the same. One assignment may involve reacting quickly to a major sports story, while the next could focus on building a search-friendly guide, supporting a partner’s coverage strategy or contributing to a live blog around a marquee event.

You will work closely with Sporting News editors to learn how content is planned, written, packaged and distributed for different audiences and platforms. You will also gain experience collaborating across departments and understanding how editorial content supports audience growth, partnerships and commercial objectives.

Throughout the internship, you will learn how Sporting News works with partners, applies SEO and audience best practices, covers major sporting events and creates content that delivers value for readers, media partners and commercial brands.

WHEN AND WHERE IS IT?

Dates: August 2026 - February 2027

Pay: $15 per hour, up to 40 hours per week

Location: Remote or Charlotte, N.C.

Apply by August 14, 2026

INTERNSHIP RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Write a high volume of clean, accurate and engaging digital content across sports, lifestyle, affiliate and partnership verticals
  • Cover breaking news and produce timely content around major stories, games and sporting events
  • Produce and manage live coverage, including live blogs, game updates and event-based content
  • Write and update evergreen articles designed to serve readers throughout the sports calendar
  • Create content for The Sporting News and its partners, including regional sports networks NESN and SportsNet Pittsburgh and other sports media brands
  • Work with editors to tailor content, tone and formatting for different audiences and publishing platforms
  • Apply SEO best practices to headlines, article structure, keyword targeting and content packaging
  • Use audience and research tools such as Google Trends and Semrush to identify story opportunities
  • Monitor sports news, schedules, trends and social conversations to generate relevant content ideas
  • Update existing articles to ensure information remains accurate, useful and timely
  • Collaborate with editors, writers and other departments to support partnership and audience-growth initiatives
  • Learn how editorial content contributes to the broader commercial value of a global sports media organization

REQUIREMENTS

  • You must be able to commit to the entire six-month program. For this reason, we consider only recent graduates who are less than 12 months removed from completing their degree
  • An ability to work quickly, accurately and efficiently in a digital news environment
  • Strong news judgment and an understanding of what makes a sports story timely, relevant and interesting
  • The ability to write clean, concise and engaging content in a variety of digital formats
  • Strong knowledge of major North American professional and collegiate sports
  • An interest in covering a variety of subjects, including sports, lifestyle, live events and affiliate content
  • A basic understanding of SEO best practices and digital audience development
  • An entrepreneurial and curious mindset with an eagerness to pitch ideas, test new approaches and learn
  • The versatility to move between breaking news, evergreen assignments and partner-specific projects
  • Strong grammar skills, meticulous attention to detail and a firm grasp of AP style
  • A willingness to work collaboratively with editors and writers and respond positively to constructive feedback
  • The ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines at the same time
  • Flexibility to work a combination of days, nights and weekends as required by the sports calendar

ABOUT SPORTING NEWS, THE COMPANY

Sporting News is more than a media brand—we are a global team of passionate sports fans delivering trusted content to audiences around the world. Founded in 1886, we have a 140-year legacy of sports journalism excellence, evolving from a print publication into a cutting-edge digital media company that serves millions of fans across multiple platforms and languages.

At our core, we believe in expert storytelling, ensuring that every piece of content we produce meets the high expectations of modern sports enthusiasts.

  • Operate with Integrity – Trust is the foundation of Sporting News, and we uphold that tradition by delivering fact-based, insightful coverage.
  • Answer with Expertise – With a deep understanding of sports and its impact, our team delivers content that is knowledgeable, analytical, and forward-thinking.
  • Deliver Consistently – Whether breaking news, in-depth analysis, or immersive storytelling, we strive to provide high-quality content that resonates with fans.
  • Trust One Another – Our global team collaborates across borders, fostering a culture of respect and inclusion.

At Sporting News, we celebrate the diversity of our team and leadership. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone—regardless of race, gender, background, or identity—can contribute, grow, and succeed.

ABOUT SPORTING NEWS, THE BRAND

Sporting News is one of the most storied and recognizable sports media brands in the world. Founded in 1886 as a U.S. weekly newspaper, it became a pioneering force in sports journalism—earning titles like "The Nation's Oldest & Finest Sports Paper" and "The Bible of Baseball."

Today, Sporting News is a digital-first, globally connected media powerhouse with localized editions in the U.S., Brazil, Canada, Mexico, Argentina, U.K., Spain, India, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia, and Japan— with more regions on the horizon.

As we approach our 140-year milestone, Sporting News remains committed to evolving with the ever-changing sports media landscape while staying true to the values that have defined us for generations.

Acquired by an international investment group in 2021 with deep sports, media and gaming experience, TSN is poised to become the first truly global digital sports media platform business.

Пропонуємо те, що має значення саме для тебе: 

  • Конкурентна заробітна плата: гарантуємо стабільний дохід. Додатково, у нас діє реферальна програма винагороди за залучення нових колег до Райффайзен Банку.
  • Соціальний пакет: офіційне працевлаштування, 28 днів оплачуваної відпустки, додатковий «декрет» для татусів, та матеріальна допомога для батьків при народженні дітей.
  • Комфортні умови праці: гібридний формат роботи у м. Івано-Франківськ або віддалений формат роботи з можливістю працювати з будь якого куточка України, забезпечення сучасною технікою.

  • Wellbeing програма: для всіх співробітників доступні медичне страхування з першого робочого дня; консультації психолога, нутриціолога чи юриста; дисконт програми на спорт та покупки; family days для дітей та дорослих; масаж в офісі.

  • Крута команда: наші колеги – це спільнота, де вітаються допитливість, талант та інновації. Ми підтримуємо один одного, вчимося разом та зростаємо. Ти можеш знайти однодумців у понад 15-ти професійних ком’юніті, читацькому чи спортивному клубах.

Для ветеранів та ветеранок у нас діє програма підтримки, розвивається ветеранська спільнота Банку. Ми працюємо над підвищенням обізнаності керівників та команд з питань повернення ветеранів до цивільного життя. Райффайзен Банк відзначений як один з найкращих роботодавців для ветеранів (Forbes).

Our current team handles day-to-day transactional processing and routine bookkeeping efficiently. However, as we advance through an active audit, a major software migration, and broader process improvement initiatives, we require a senior-level technical expert. Your primary focus will not be high-volume transactional work, but rather providing the deep accounting judgment, rigorous review capabilities, and control structures needed to ensure absolute technical accuracy and audit readiness.

You will partner directly with leadership to bridge the gap between day-to-day operations and high-level strategic financial oversight.


Key Responsibilities & Challenges to Solve

Technical GAAP & Specialized Accounting

  • Lease Accounting (ASC 842): Take full ownership of the review and ongoing management of Right-of-Use (ROU) assets and lease liabilities. Assess new contracts and modifications, ensuring all documentation is robust and audit-ready.

  • Fixed Assets & Capitalization: Oversee PPE accounting, refine and enforce capitalization policies, manage asset disposals, evaluate impairment considerations, and ensure the fixed asset register is flawlessly maintained.

  • Technical GAAP Review: Act as the critical second line of defense. Review complex transactions, contract assessments, and financing arrangements, making definitive accounting treatment decisions before they become audit findings.

Controllership, Month-End, & Oversight

  • Month-End Close & Accruals: Partner with leadership to strengthen accrual methodologies, strictly enforce cut-off procedures, and significantly reduce the manual adjustments identified during close.

  • Balance Sheet Reconciliations & Controls: Establish and enforce elevated reconciliation standards, design stronger review controls, and foster clear ownership across all key accounts.

  • Audit Management & Documentation: Prepare detailed audit schedules, reports, and technical documentation for review by management and external auditors, ensuring full compliance with US GAAP standards.

Process Improvement & System Transformation

  • System Migration & Workflow Design: Active partner in our upcoming software migration. Document current processes, identify internal control gaps, redesign workflows, and ensure complex accounting requirements are accurately mapped into the new system.

  • Fraud Prevention & Risk Mitigation: Continually assess financial risk, investigate discrepancies, and implement improvements to internal control systems to prevent errors and fraud.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and required experience with QuickBooks Online. Experience with NetSuite is preferred, along with familiarity navigating complex accounting systems and software migrations

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field is required.

  • Certification: CPA or CIA designation is highly preferred.

  • Execution: Strong organizational skills with a meticulous attention to detail. Ability to work independently, manage shifting timelines, and thrive in a fully remote environment.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Indiana at Teach Plus
jobs.excerpt: What We DoTeach Plus is a national nonprofit whose mission is to empower excellent, experienced, and diverse teachers to take leadership over key policy and practice issues that advance equity, opportunity, and student success.
jobs.description:
What We Do

Teach Plus is a national nonprofit whose mission is to empower excellent, experienced, and diverse teachers to take leadership over key policy and practice issues that advance equity, opportunity, and student success. At the heart of our work is developing teacher leadership and voice in pursuit of student outcomes. We believe that investing in our most talented teachers—developing them into well-informed, persuasive leaders—gives them deep leverage in elevating the most pressing education issues facing students, teachers, and communities while advancing opportunities for students. Learn more at .

Teach Plus Executive Director Role

At Teach Plus, our Student Opportunity Mandate calls us to seek long-term, measurable, and structural change on behalf of students, communities, and educators. Reporting to the Chief Regional Impact and Operations Officer, Executive Directors (EDs) at Teach Plus are responsible for setting the vision and executing on strategies to drive this local impact in the states where we work. As sophisticated systems leaders and subject matter experts, Teach Plus EDs are convicted and credible power brokers that strategically advance bodies of work that address the most critical needs for students, communities, and educators. While this role has foundational responsibilities and required skills, mindsets, and orientations, it is ultimately a highly contextualized, hyper-local systems leadership role that requires an ongoing analysis of the role Executives and the broader institution (Teach Plus) must play in a community at any given time. This role is Indiana-based with regular in-state travel; occasional national travel as needed.

The Foundational Executive Director Responsibilities Include:

  1. Setting a Vision for Local Impact, Grounded in Strategic Clarity: Through an iterative approach, Executive Directors must be able to continuously:
    • Understand and describe (both internally to the organization and to external partners) evidence and case studies of prior student outcomes improvement, the drivers that led to this success, and the patterns around those drivers as they specifically relate to advocacy and teacher leadership
    • Concretely articulate the gaps between the current state of student outcomes and the aspirations of students, families, and communities, and set ambitious goals/and or strategies to close these gaps, centered on tangible outcomes for students
    • In partnership with other organizations and coalition members, develop a sophisticated theory of change and theory of action/logic model around what is required to advance these student outcomes goals and the particular role Teach Plus (teachers, alumni, Executive, and institution) must play as a result
  1. Advancing Teacher Leadership, Voice, and Advocacy towards our Student Opportunity Mandate: In partnership with Center teams at Teach Plus and local partners, EDs must:
    • Establish and continuously evolve local models for teacher learning and leadership aligned with Teach Plus’s Leadership Attribute Continuum and Policy Attributes and Competencies
    • In partnership with the Center and external partners, use sophisticated data, measurement, and evaluation structures to continuously assess and improve teacher engagement models, including accountability models for managing staff towards effective execution of these programs
      1. Identify best practices for language, expectations, implementation, and accountability across policy and practice programs to support quality programming.
    • Through iterative strategic clarity work, co-create and effectively invest educators in a sophisticated annual or multi-year policy agenda, focused on advancing our Student Opportunity Mandate
    • Co-create and revise contextualized local curricula and learning experiences to prepare teachers to engage directly with influential lawmakers, stakeholders, and government employees around your local policy agenda, ultimately positioning them to serve as effective leaders throughout their careers
    • Leverage insights from strategic clarity and evidence-based strategies to run and participate in sophisticated local and state advocacy campaigns
    • In partnership with the Communications, Research, and other External Affairs teams, develop a robust and sophisticated strategy for developing teachers as trusted messengers and elevating teacher voice in the media in alignment with your strategic clarity work and policy agenda
    • Develop teacher leadership and foster cross-sector collaboration to align education with community and business needs in areas such as literacy, college and career readiness, and other potential drivers.
  1. Creating and Stewarding a Network of Champions: In partnership with Teach Plus’ broader institutional positioning strategy, EDs must:
    • Set and execute against an ambitious annual fundraising goal-ranging from $350,000 to $2M, given local context-through a highly intentional portfolio management partnership with our national External Affairs team.
    • Strategically create, join, and strengthen local coalitions with a clear understanding of Teach Plus’ value add
    • Develop, share, and continuously refine student and teacher-centered stories that can be leveraged to invest and grow the network of champions
    • Attract, retain, and steward a diverse portfolio of donors to both meet/exceed annual fundraising goals and continuously elevate Teach Plus’-and your own role in the broader ecosystem
    • In partnership with Regional Development Directors and/or your team, ensure fundraising deliverables are high quality, aligned to your local strategy, and delivered to partners in a timely and effective manner
    • Build a cabinet of subject matter experts, funders and/or local leaders (at times, this will be Senior Fellows and/or a Local Advisory Board) to continuously improve your executive positioning, local visibility, and access to cutting-edge insights and innovations
    • In partnership with the Center, create a fundraising toolkit of resources that can be leveraged in a variety of ways for ongoing fundraising opportunities, including but not limited to: one-pagers, visuals, and language for funder emails.
  1. Creating and Sustaining Enabling Conditions for Impact: As the highest impact level towards local impact at Teach Plus, EDs must:
    • Build out, hire, retain, train, and continuously “right size” a local staffing model, grounded in their Strategic Clarity work-in particular, the role Teach Plus must play in the local ecosystem. In partnership with the People team, ensure that role profiles for staff, Senior Fellows, and/or contractors are aligned to a rigorous Vision of Excellence.
    • Serve as exemplary People Managers, regardless of staffing size, through a high-candor, coaching-first culture and effective communication of expectations, including but not limited to supporting direct reports to set and execute against Visions of Excellence and Annual Goals
    • In partnership with the Center, co-create plans for local staff learning and development, aligned with regional strategy, annual goals, and performance management needs
    • Set and manage against an annual regional expense target, partnering with the Central finance and your team to balance compliance with original budgets as well as responsiveness and iteration as strategy evolves in-year
    • Grounded in our commitment to “Reimagine the Center” operate with both candor and empathy to strategically maximize Central staff and resources to increase local impact

To effectively execute on these four core responsibilities, in addition to the roles they play in their unique communities, we believe all successful EDs must embody the following:

MINDSETS AND ORIENTATIONS:

  1. Embodying systems leadership. This includes:
    • The ability to see the larger system-constantly evaluating and adapting your mental models, interrogating your preconceived notions and remaining open to new ideas/information, including data sets and evolving evidence bases
    • Building trust and shifting conversations by fostering reflection and more generative conversations. Not only does this mean doing so in groups and in community, but also continuously “locating yourself” in regards to your own consciousness and orientations to change.
    • Prioritizing co-creating the future while maintaining the ability to be responsive to current circumstances. This requires simultaneously holding both a deep understanding and conviction around current systems' failure and inspiring yourself and others to seek new solutions.
    • Understanding the way systemic inequity and oppression serve as the root cause for not only external challenges, but in many interpersonal interactions and group dynamics. Always operating from a deep knowledge of how your own identity impacts your leadership and how others experience it.
  2. An unyielding focus on equitable student outcomes. This looks/sounds like:
    • Maintaining a deep understanding of the current state of student outcomes across their state, not just in major hubs or the dominant conversations/pundit talking points.
    • Always tying regional decisions to a theory of action (how x decision will ultimately increase y student outcome), even through multiple layers of staff or teacher leaders.
    • Establishing credibility with state and district partners who can speak to unique proof points, trends, and outliers in the student outcomes landscape.
    • Keeping a pulse on the broader national conversation re: student outcomes and understanding the unique role your state is/isn’t playing in the dialogue.
  3. A focus on building the systems leadership of teachers as nuanced navigators of the education landscape.
    • Recognizing and articulating the unique role that teacher perspective and experience play in advocating for and advancing systems change
    • Affirming individual teacher lived experiences while simultaneously supporting them to operate as systems leaders who can observe and make meaning of the broader ecosystem
    • Belief that narrative (op-eds, teacher stories, testimony, etc) has and can play a significant role in change efforts, locally and nationally
    • Constantly balancing robust teacher input mechanisms with your own personal conviction and student/family aspirations when setting and driving towards a strategy
  4. A solutions orientation. This looks/sounds like:
    • Assuming that problems have multiple, complex solutions and using your available resources to address them proactively, collaboratively, and creatively
    • Communicating directly with those impacted by/informing the challenges you face, leveraging radical candor to ensure all parties are clear on the challenge and aligned on the most efficacious approach to solving it
    • Taking a long-term view and recognizing that 90% of the time taken to address a challenge should be spent on problem analysis and understanding the root cause, especially of persistent or recurring challenges

SKILLS:

  • Set and continuously evaluate strategies for local impact, closely aligned to quantitative and qualitative goals
  • Effectively communicate org vision and strategy to internal (Teach Plus) and external partners to advance work
  • Leverage and grow professional networks to facilitate the effective positioning of Teach Plus amongst other organizations and groups in your ecosystem
  • Build and/or leverage existing systems to ensure operational excellence (meeting deadlines, prioritizing time) for yourself and those you manage
  • Identifying and developing talent, both in your team and in teacher leaders, in such a way that fosters recruitment, matriculation, retention, and tangible success
  • Managing individuals towards agreed-upon, measurable outcomes using both formal performance management and routine coaching structures
  • Leveraging data sets and multiple platforms (Martus, Salesforce, etc) to effectively track, analyze, and act on your ongoing knowledge of progress to goal(s)
  • Understanding and managing financial information, including Budget-to-Actuals and grant reports
  • Ability to track and analyze key policies in your landscape and take aligned action with local partners/your Fellows and network
  • Speaking and writing in ways that effectively convey key information and/or bring others into deeper partnership, including but not limited to fundraising
  • Ability to inspire and motivate others through storytelling, crafting compelling narratives that resonate with multiple audiences and highlight the org’s mission and impact
  • Serving as an exemplary people manager through team leadership, community building, and mobilizing others
  • Communicating with radical candor and using principles of nonviolent communication to foster compassionate and effective communication, leading to better understanding and collaboration.

Location, Travel, and Commitment

This is a full-time (40 hours/week) remote position for candidates who reside in Indiana and are willing to travel to Indianapolis during the legislative session, and periodically to other parts of the state. The role requires a flexible schedule, including some nights and weekends, to support policy sessions and meet with teachers and policymakers. The anticipated start date is September 2026.

Compensation and Benefits

The base salary is $140,000, with defined opportunities for increased compensation through a merit-based annual bonus opportunity and/or increasing annual revenue targets. Teach Plus provides a comprehensive benefits package and time-off, including 15 vacation days, 3 personal days, 5 sick days, 13 holidays, July break, Winter break, paid parental leave, and a 4-week paid sabbatical for every five years of service.

CVX Venture Scout Programme

Do you have a passion for sourcing investments and making a difference for growth companies? Do you want to assist an extraordinary team of talented, motivated, driven individuals who all share a deep passion for entrepreneurship? If so, you may be our new Venture Scout. Please note, this is not a full time role, but we will provide remuneration based on success criteria.

Introduction

The CVX Venture Scout Programme is building a network of highly talented VC scouts, to assist us in sourcing attractive investment opportunities, in their specialist fields. You will learn and develop some of the most important skills required to be in VC, and meet with some of the most interesting and entrepreneurial founders in your market, and help shape the future.

As part of your role as a CVX Venture Scout, the Investment Team will look to you to identify exciting startups, speak with them and conduct research on them, including their teams, markets, and competition. Based on your findings, you will write a 1-2 page proposal memo summarising your investment thesis, and may be asked to present it in-person or online to the CVX Investment Team.

Expectations

We aim to use our Venture Scout Programme not only to discover exceptional investment opportunities but also to gain a deeper understanding of you and your vision. If you are interested in joining the CVX Investment Team, this is an excellent first step towards not only gaining an introduction to the VC ecosystem and learning essential VC skills, but also demonstrating how you think about investments, analyse them, and present your insights to us. As we grow our Investment Team, the Venture Scout Programme will be the first pool of resource we look to hire from.

Compensation

We want to remunerate good work and give credit to your role in the investment process, where successful. We will therefore compensate you when a deal that you take forward to the investment team receives funding from our network of investors, with an opportunity for you to benefit from the upside too.

Our Mission

CVX is one of Europe's fastest-growing venture investors, and we help ambitious and promising growth companies reach their full potential by investing capital, knowledge, time, skills, and network. We are driven by our conviction that the best investors are often those who, in addition to capital, provide founders with the right knowledge and experiences, skills, and networks in relation to the stage and industry in which the company operates. CVX always invests together with the best business angels for the respective founder, and today we have over 700 partners in our network who invest in companies and bring their skills into play where they can really add value.

The CVX Venture Scout Programme is building a network of highly talented VC scouts, to assist us in sourcing attractive investment opportunities, in their specialist fields. CVX is one of Europe's fastest-growing venture investors, and we help ambitious and promising growth companies reach their full potential by investing capital, knowledge, time, skills, and network. About Somethings

Somethings is building the first social wellness platform for teens — a place where a teen can form a real relationship with a mentor who gets them, sticks with them, and helps them get better.
